'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Myanmar civil war (2021–present)|Myanmar civil war]]
**A [[Myanmar Air Force]] fighter jet strikes a village near [[Bhamo]] in [[Kachin State]], [[Myanmar]], killing 21 people and wounding 28 others. [https://apnews.com/article/myanmar-airstrike-bhamo-hteelin-village-21-killed-7b8a56ad60d7d5282ac28f9681b751aa (AP)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[98th Academy Awards]]
**Nominations for the 2025 [[Academy Awards]] are released, with ''[[Sinners (2025 film)|Sinners]]'' receiving 16 overall nominations, surpassing the record for most nominations for a film that was previously held by ''[[All About Eve]]'' ([[23rd Academy Awards|1950]]), ''[[Titanic (1997 film)|Titanic]]'' ([[70th Academy Awards|1997]]), and ''[[La La Land]]'' ([[89th Academy Awards|2016]]). [https://www.dw.com/en/sinners-breaks-records-at-2026-oscar-nominations/a-75606280 (DW)] [https://www.latimes.com/entertainment-arts/awards/story/2026-01-22/oscar-nominations-2026-list-nominees (''Los Angeles Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[South Korea]]'s benchmark [[KOSPI]] [[Stock market index|index]] surpasses 5,000 points for the first time, rising by more than two percent in [[Extended-hours trading|early trading]]. [https://gulfnews.com/business/markets/south-koreas-benchmark-kospi-breaks-5000-for-the-first-time-1.500416569 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2026 Gul Plaza Shopping Mall fire]]
**The death toll from a massive fire five days ago at a multi-story [[shopping mall]] in [[Karachi]], [[Sindh]], [[Pakistan]], increases to 67 people. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/world/article/death-toll-in-pakistan-shopping-plaza-fire-rises-to-67-officials-say/ (AP via CTV News)]
*[[January 2026 New Zealand storms]]
**Two people are killed and several others are reported missing with no sign of life detected, including children, in [[landslide]]s in [[Mount Maunganui]] and [[Welcome Bay]], [[Tauranga]], [[New Zealand]]. Further north, a man is swept away by a [[flood]] in [[Warkworth, New Zealand|Warkworth]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/c0erdp8q1qyt (BBC News)] [https://news.sky.com/story/several-missing-after-new-zealand-campsite-landslide-with-no-sign-of-life-detected-for-hours-official-says-13497417 (Sky News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/australasia/new-zealand-floods-mount-maunganui-landslide-latest-updates-b2905363.html (''The Independent'')]
*[[January 2026 North American winter storm]]
**A [[state of emergency]] is declared in several [[United States|U.S.]] [[U.S. state|states]] in anticipation for a potentially severe [[winter storm]] affecting the [[Southern United States|South]] and [[Eastern United States]], [[Atlantic Canada]], and [[Northern Mexico]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/science/us-winter-storm-explained-9.7054574 (CBC)]
*[[Vanderbijlpark scholar transport crash]]
**The death toll from the [[school bus]] collision with a truck near [[Vanderbijlpark]], [[Gauteng]], [[South Africa]], increases to 14 children killed, while the bus driver is charged with [[murder]]. [https://apnews.com/article/south-africa-school-bus-crash-accident-912ab2141d19b13d8f02ae38994f55a6 (AP)]
*[[Mozambique]] authorities report at least 13 deaths from flooding caused by heavy rains, which has affected more than 500,000 people. [https://www.reuters.com/sustainability/climate-energy/mozambique-counts-13-dead-floods-so-far-toll-expected-rise-2026-01-22/ (Reuters)]
*Ten people are killed and ten injured after a vehicle carrying army soldiers skids off a road and falls into a gorge in [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]], [[India]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/india-news/4-army-personnel-killed-9-injured-as-vehicle-falls-into-gorge-in-jammu-and-kashmirs-doda-10828692 (NDTV)]
*At least seven people are killed and more than eight others are injured in a suspected [[gas explosion]] near [[Tumaco]] in [[Nariño Department]], [[Colombia]]. [https://news.az/news/explosion-in-southern-colombia-kills-seven (News.Az)]
*Six people are lightly injured when a passenger train collides with a crane arm in [[Cartagena (Spain)|Cartagena]], [[Region of Murcia|Murcia]], [[Spain]], in the fourth railway incident in the country within a week. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/train-crashes-against-crane-southeastern-spain-tve-reports-2026-01-22/ (Reuters)]
*One person is killed and 109 schoolchildren are injured in a [[head-on collision]] between a pick-up truck and a school bus on [[R510 (South Africa)|R510]] in [[Thabazimbi Local Municipality|Thabazimbi]], [[Limpopo]], [[South Africa]]. [https://iol.co.za/news/crime-and-courts/2026-01-22-one-dead-109-pupils-injured-in-limpopo-school-bus-crash/ (IOL)]

*The [[JAMA|Journal of the American Medical Association]] reports that [[colorectal cancer]] is the leading cause of [[cancer]] death in people under 50 in the [[United States]]. '''International relations'''
*[[2021 Guinean coup d'état]]
**The [[African Union]] lifts sanctions on [[Guinea]] and restores its [[Member states of the African Union|membership]], citing progress in the country's [[Politics of Guinea|political transition]] which culminated in [[Mamady Doumbouya]]'s  [[2025 Guinean presidential election|election]] as [[President of Guinea|president]]. [https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/01/african-union-says-lifting-sanctions-against-guinea/ (AFP via ''Vanguard'')]
*[[Colombia–Ecuador relations]]
**[[Colombia]] suspends [[Electricity sector in Colombia|electricity exports]] to [[Ecuador]] and announces a 30% [[tariff]] on selected [[Economy of Ecuador|Ecuadorian goods]] to [[Reciprocity (international relations)|reciprocate]] Ecuador's imposition of the same surcharge on [[Economy of Colombia|Colombian imports]] effective February 1, which [[President of Ecuador|Ecuadorian president]] [[Daniel Noboa]] attributed to a [[trade deficit]] and a lack of cooperation ‌on [[War on drugs|combating drug trafficking]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/colombia-suspends-electricity-sales-imposes-30-tariff-ecuador-escalating-trade-2026-01-22/ (Reuters)]
*[[France–Russia relations]]
**The [[France|French]] [[French Navy|Navy]] boards and seizes a [[Russia]]n [[Russian shadow fleet|shadow fleet]] [[oil tanker]] subject to international sanctions in the [[Mediterranean Sea]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/1/22/france-seizes-oil-tanker-in-mediterranean-sailing-from-russia-macron (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Proposals for the United States to withdraw from the United Nations]]
**The [[United States]]'s [[Executive Order 14155|withdrawal]] from the [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) takes effect, becoming the first member state to leave the WHO. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/us-set-quit-world-health-organization-2026-01-22/ (Reuters)]

The shooter is at large. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2026/jan/22/three-people-dead-after-shooting-in-nsw-town-lake-cargelligo-as-police-urge-locals-to-stay-inside-ntwnfb (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c4g00mv29j5o (BBC News)]

**Three people are killed, including the perpetrator, and another is critically injured in a [[school shooting]] at a [[primary school]] in [[Ntabankulu Local Municipality|Ntabankulu]], [[Eastern Cape]], [[South Africa]]. [https://iol.co.za/news/crime-and-courts/2026-01-22-update-former-teachers-attack-leaves-two-dead-after-shooting-at-ntabankulu-primary-school/ (Independent Online)]
*[[Terrorism in the Philippines]]
**A [[Regional Trial Court|regional court]] in [[Tacloban]], [[Leyte]], [[Philippines]], sentences journalist [[Frenchie Mae Cumpio]] and her accomplice to up to 18 years in prison for [[Terrorism financing|financing terrorism]] following their arrest in 2020, but acquits them on [[Criminal possession of a weapon|a weapons possession charge]]. [[Mass media in the Philippines|Press freedom]] and [[Human rights in the Philippines|rights groups]] condemn the verdict. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/22/frenchie-mae-cumpio-philippine-journalist-found-guilty (AFP via ''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cr7jjnl49nro (BBC News)]
*Six people are injured, including two critically, in a [[mass stabbing]] during a [[Kurds|Kurdish]] demonstration in [[Antwerp]], [[Flanders]], [[Belgium]]. Two suspects are arrested. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/jan/22/six-injured-after-knife-attack-at-kurdish-demonstration-in-antwerp-belgium (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Canada|Canadian]] drug trafficker and fugitive [[Ryan Wedding]], who is on the [[FBI Most Wanted List]], is arrested in [[Mexico]]. [https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/ap-report-ryan-wedding-elite-snowboarder-turned-most-wanted-drug-trafficking-fugitive-arrested-in-mexico (PBS)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]], [[Regulation of artificial intelligence]], [[Science and technology in South Korea]]
**[[South Korea]] enacts a [[Law of South Korea|law]] that requires human oversight of high-impact [[artificial intelligence]] (AI) systems, mandates disclosure and labeling of certain AI uses, and institutes fines of up to [[South Korean won|₩]]30 million (around [[United States dollar|US$]]20,400) for violations. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/south-korea-launches-landmark-laws-regulate-ai-startups-warn-compliance-burdens-2026-01-22/ (Reuters)]
